articles.title: Home Assistant builds a bootable installer for ordinary PCs
articles.dek: A prepared USB stick installs Home Assistant OS without needing a network connection on the target computer.
body: Home Assistant’s installer adds a bootable USB route for generic x86-64 PCs. Another computer prepares the stick, then the target PC boots from it and installs Home Assistant OS onto a selected internal disk. The target computer needs no network connection during installation; creating the stick still needs internet access.

The installer can also save a bootable ISO for virtual machines or other writing tools. Its full-screen interface offers a disk chooser, progress and next steps. Installation requires typing “erase”, and the selected disk’s identity is checked again immediately before writing.
The route requires UEFI with Secure Boot disabled. Tests cover a Dell OptiPlex with a SATA drive and virtual machines; installations onto NVMe or eMMC have not yet been checked on hardware.

pullRequests.title: UI - add live USB installer for generic x86-64 (PoC)
Give the live USB installer a full-screen interface

media.alt: Home Assistant’s live USB installer asks which disk to install onto.

articles.title: ESPHome connects devices beyond Wi-Fi through cellular modems
articles.dek: A wired modem gives an ESP32 a data connection for its existing network services.
body: ESPHome adds cellular networking for ESP32 devices connected to a compatible modem over a serial cable. Makers can use its normal API, MQTT messaging and firmware-update services over the mobile data connection where Wi-Fi or Ethernet is unavailable.

Olivier ARCHER supplies support for SIMCom, Quectel BG96 and generic AT-command modems. The connection keeps modem commands working while data is flowing. An incorrect SIM PIN stops the modem instead of repeatedly trying it and risking a locked SIM.
The first component supplies networking. Satellite positioning, modem power management and signal sensors remain separate work; it cannot be configured alongside ESPHome’s Ethernet component.

pullRequests.title: [modem] Add PPPoS networking over a UART cellular modem on ESP32
Modem component documentation

articles.title: Piper cuts the wait for speech in native applications
articles.dek: Optional streaming gives screen-reader applications their first audio before the whole sentence is ready.
body: Piper’s native speech library starts returning audio before it has synthesized an entire sentence. Applications such as screen readers can begin speaking sooner when they adopt the updated library and prepare a voice for streaming.

In a test using a rebuilt Piper macOS app on an Apple M3 running macOS 26, the first audio buffer for a six-second sentence arrived after 0.24 seconds instead of 4.15. The measurement used the speech-extension path used by VoiceOver and wrote audio to files; it measured buffer delivery, rather than sound reaching a listener.

The change also lets the library use several processor cores. Streaming requires a voice split into two model files with the supplied tool; ordinary voices keep sentence-at-a-time output. Contributor herwigfelix makes a first contribution to Piper with the work.

pullRequests.title: Stream audio from libpiper for split voices and use several threads

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps Jellyfin sign-in tokens out of library data
articles.dek: Track links and artwork had exposed the connected Jellyfin account’s access token to library readers.
body: Music Assistant stops sending the connected Jellyfin account’s access token to everyone who can read its music library. The token appeared inside track and artwork addresses returned to clients, potentially exposing an account with administrator privileges.

Marvin Schenkel replaces the track address with Jellyfin’s ordinary details page and adds artwork credentials only on the server, for the configured Jellyfin host. Existing library rows can still contain the old token; Jellyfin invalidates it when the provider signs in again using its existing device identity.

pullRequests.title: Stop exposing the Jellyfin access token to API clients

articles.title: Home Assistant restricts conversations to the person who started them
articles.dek: Knowing another conversation’s identifier stops being enough to continue it.
body: Home Assistant stops one signed-in user from continuing another person’s conversation merely by supplying its identifier. Previously, that could carry over the conversation’s history and tools.
The first input gives the conversation an owner, and subsequent user input must come from the same person. Internal callers that supply no user input retain their existing access to conversations.

pullRequests.title: Only let the user who started a conversation continue it

articles.title: ZHA reduces the risk of new light groups inheriting old members
articles.dek: New group identifiers avoid immediately reusing a deleted group’s address.
body: ZHA changes how it assigns addresses to new Zigbee groups, reducing the chance that a supposedly removed light responds to a new group’s commands. A device that was offline during deletion can retain its old group address; the previous allocator promptly reused that address.

New groups receive a randomly chosen unused address instead. This also makes it less likely that Home Assistant restores a deleted group’s name, area or labels onto the new group. Existing groups keep their addresses, and reuse remains possible rather than being eliminated.

Companion checks reject duplicate group names, addresses already in use and invalid members before creating a group. Showing those specific errors in Home Assistant’s interface requires separate work.

pullRequests.title: Allocate Zigbee group IDs at random instead of filling gaps
Raise instead of silently failing when creating a Zigbee group

articles.title: Music Assistant’s phone player adds a 24-bit audio option
articles.dek: The lossless setting supports Android 12 and newer, plus iOS, while retaining 16-bit fallback.
body: Music Assistant’s phone player adds an optional 24-bit setting for lossless FLAC and uncompressed PCM audio. It supports Android 12 and newer and iOS; Opus playback remains 16-bit, and the new option starts off.

Andrii Mitnovych also makes FLAC the default for new installations while preserving the previous Opus default for existing setups. The player offers stereo audio at 48 kHz and keeps a 16-bit fallback. The setting expands the phone player’s audio formats; it does not promise an audible improvement from every phone or output device.

pullRequests.title: Hi-Res Sendspin (24bit support)

articles.title: Home Assistant gives AI troubleshooting a fuller system timeline
articles.dek: A connected assistant can inspect integration failures alongside logs from the host and installed apps.
body: Home Assistant gives connected AI assistants a fuller timeline for investigating a failure. The system-management connection adds full logs around a chosen time, extending the recent warnings and errors it already supplied.

On systems with Supervisor, the tools cover Home Assistant, Supervisor, host, plugin and app logs; other installations use the log file. A companion read-only tool lists installed integration connections, filters their loading status and supplies their translated error reasons.

These tools belong to the administrator-only Home Assistant management connection. Selecting it can share the requested logs with the configured AI provider; its access is broader than the household entities normally exposed to Assist.

pullRequests.title: Add LLM tools to query the full logs
Add GetConfigEntriesTool LLM tool to config integration
Add Home Assistant LLM API and system log tool

articles.title: Z-Wave JS limits requests that can stall a network
articles.dek: Bounds on radio tests and security challenges prevent runaway traffic and a frozen driver.
body: Z-Wave JS limits two kinds of incoming requests that could leave a network busy or unresponsive. A radio-test request must target a known device other than the controller, cannot request more than one thousand test frames, and cannot restart a test already running.

The driver also caps outstanding challenges used by the older S0 security protocol. A flood of requests could previously exhaust every challenge identifier and trap the driver in an endless search for a free one. At the new limit it refuses the additional request instead.

pullRequests.title: fix: validate incoming Powerlevel Test Node Set commands
fix: limit the number of outstanding S0 nonces

articles.title: ESPHome controls Delta wallbox charging over Bluetooth
articles.dek: A local connection starts and stops sessions and reads power, energy and charging time.
body: ESPHome adds a Bluetooth connection to Delta AC wallboxes, letting makers start or stop a charging session and read the charger’s state, power, energy and charging time. The connection also exposes the charger’s model, serial number and firmware versions.

The component pairs and signs in with the configured PIN and password before polling. An optional time source keeps the charger’s clock in step. The accompanying guide covers finding its Bluetooth address and configuring the readings and controls.

pullRequests.title: [delta_wallbox] Delta AC wallbox
Delta wallbox documentation

articles.title: Music Assistant 2.10.8 restores blocked Apple Music connections
articles.dek: A saved application token expired on October 22, blocking setups created before Music Assistant 2.10.
body: Music Assistant 2.10.8 restores Apple Music connections blocked by an expired application token saved in older setups. The failure began on October 22 for installations configured before version 2.10; signing in again did not replace the stale copy, so the connection still failed to load.

Marvin Schenkel makes the connection choose whichever application token expires later: the saved one or the copy bundled with Music Assistant. A test against Apple using the expired saved token changed the rejected request into a successful connection.

pullRequests.title: Fix Apple Music failing to load with an expired stored app token
[Backport to stable] 2.10.8

articles.title: Matter.js Server controls Yeelight Cube Lite displays
articles.dek: Device-specific controls add drawings, animated images and music effects through the server.
body: Matter.js Server adds controls for the Yeelight Cube Lite’s light matrix, including effects, drawings, animated GIF uploads and microphone-driven music mode. Previously, the server could read its manufacturer-specific attributes but refused writes and commands.

Max-src tested the controls on a Cube Lite running firmware 1.12.32, including an animation uploaded and played on the lamp. The work also adds display-direction, module-layout and button-playlist controls. These are server and client-interface capabilities, not new Home Assistant dashboard controls.

pullRequests.title: Add Yeelight Cube Lite custom clusters (0x1312FC00-FC11)

articles.title: Home Assistant retires the old Telegram notification setup
articles.dek: Automations using legacy notification actions need to move to Telegram bot notify entities.
body: Home Assistant removes the legacy Telegram notify platform, ending its named notification actions. Existing YAML entries receive a repair notice directing owners to the Telegram bot integration.

Each chat ID should be added as a Telegram bot subentry, with ordinary messages sent through notify.send_message. Telegram bot’s own actions remain the route for photos, documents, keyboards and other options. The old platform: telegram entries also need to be removed from the notify section of configuration.yaml.

pullRequests.title: Remove the deprecated Telegram notify integration
Remove the Telegram integration documentation

articles.title: Home Assistant guides Nest owners through the November event migration
articles.dek: A warning and reconfiguration flow replace removing and rebuilding the connection.
body: Home Assistant adds a repair warning for Nest connections still using Google’s hosted event topics, which Google is retiring on November 30. Affected owners are directed to Reconfigure, where they can select or create a topic in their own Google Cloud project without removing the integration.

The reconfiguration flow keeps a valid sign-in and the current selections where possible. A separate error flags a missing event subscription instead of leaving the connection without guidance. This puts an in-app route behind the migration advice published earlier this month.

pullRequests.title: Add repair issues for Nest Pub/Sub topic migration and missing subscription
Add reconfigure flow for Nest Pub/Sub topic and subscription

articles.title: Home Assistant gives Tuya irrigation channels proper valve controls
articles.dek: Existing multi-channel switches have a migration deadline of May 2027.
body: Home Assistant gives supported Tuya irrigation devices water-valve controls for opening and closing the supply. Single-channel devices using the standard switch control gain a valve, including the GIEX Watering Timer.

Multi-channel irrigation controllers gain a separate “Channel N” device for each indexed valve. Their former numbered switches are deprecated for removal in Home Assistant 2027.5. Existing enabled switches keep working with a repair notice; owners should move dashboards and automations to the valves, then disable the old switches.

articles.title: ESPHome restores spoken replies after fast voice recognition
articles.dek: Devices sharing one audio connection stop holding the microphone open when it is time to answer.
body: ESPHome fixes a failure in which a voice assistant heard a request but never spoke its answer. With a fast speech-recognition engine, response events could arrive before the microphone had actually stopped, leaving it in control of the audio connection the speaker needed.

The device waits for the microphone to stop before starting its reply. The correction was tested on an ESP32-S3-BOX-3 with its ready-made voice-assistant configuration and addresses the failure seen with Home Assistant Link’s second-generation speech recognition.

pullRequests.title: [voice_assistant] Wait for microphone to stop before speaking response

articles.title: Home Assistant reads Apple Fitness goals and stand hours
articles.dek: Optional iPhone sensors let dashboards use real ring targets instead of guessed ones.
body: Home Assistant’s iPhone app adds Move, Exercise and Stand goals alongside the day’s stand hours from Apple Health. These read-only, opt-in sensors let a dashboard compare progress with the targets used by Apple’s Fitness rings.

Exercise and Stand values require an Apple Watch and appear unavailable without the required data. Goals retain the latest recorded summary across midnight, while stand hours follow the current day. The contributor checked all four readings against Fitness on an iPhone paired with an Apple Watch.

pullRequests.title: Add Apple Health ring goals and stand hours sensors
Document Apple Health activity ring goals and stand hours

articles.title: Home Assistant’s Matter map shows devices behind bridges
articles.dek: Expandable bridges reveal the connected devices that previously disappeared from the map.
body: Home Assistant’s Matter network map adds devices connected through a bridge, such as a FRITZ!Smart Gateway. A bridge displays its device count and expands when selected, revealing the endpoints that the old map omitted.

The devices can be searched and opened directly. Their connecting lines carry no signal-strength claim because they are not Matter radio links; the lines become dashed when the bridge is offline. Disabled devices stay hidden.

pullRequests.title: Show bridged devices on the Matter network map

articles.title: Home Assistant extends camera talkback to Matter
articles.dek: Compatible Matter cameras join the new opt-in audio preview.
body: Home Assistant adds two-way audio support for compatible Matter cameras. This extends the camera Talk feature introduced with Reolink support to the Matter connection, beyond its earlier live video and snapshots.
Talk remains an opt-in Home Assistant Labs preview and requires a compatible camera and WebRTC stream. Browsers require HTTPS for microphone access.

pullRequests.title: Support two-way audio for Matter cameras

articles.title: Home Assistant changes how handwritten event offsets choose before or after
articles.dek: Some YAML sun and calendar triggers need their offset sign reversed.
body: Home Assistant makes negative offsets run before a sun or calendar event and positive offsets run after it. Anyone who wrote a sun.* or calendar.event_started or calendar.event_ended trigger with an offset but no offset_type needs to reverse the sign to preserve its timing.

Triggers created through the interface already stored an explicit before-or-after choice and keep working. The editor brings that choice into the offset field, while existing configurations with offset_type remain accepted.

pullRequests.title: Use a signed offset in sun and calendar triggers
Use the offset duration mode for sun and calendar offsets
Document the signed offset of sun and calendar triggers

articles.title: UniFi Protect doorbell automations need event entities
articles.dek: Doorbell and last-event sensors are scheduled for removal in January 2027.
body: Home Assistant deprecates UniFi Protect’s doorbell binary sensor and the camera’s last-ring and last-motion sensors for removal in 2027.1. Owners should use the doorbell and motion-detection event entities instead; a repair lists automations and scripts that still refer to the old sensors.

New installations and newly added cameras no longer receive these sensors. Unlike the setup controls and health readings already scheduled for removal, these doorbell and motion signals have replacement event entities.

roadmapUpdates.summary: Matt Beauchamp Buck says the proposed cover controls allow a persistent percentage display and use a consistent frame for different device illustrations. He connects the design to a wider visual-language project; the cover opportunity remains Approved.
